svg.title: iOS · Import from device · copying · portrait
svg.desc: Mirrors App/ProjectTransferImportView.swift (transferring phase) over Shared/ProjectTransferClient.swift. The payload is file by file — `project.json` (generated in memory on the serving device, so it never touches its disk) then `source/`, `blends/` and `notes/` in name order — landing in <StorageRoot>/Incoming/<source project id>/ as `<name>.part` and renamed on completion: the rename IS the commit, so a truncated file can never be mistaken for a whole one. Both byte counts are uncompressed and nothing on this path is compressed, so unlike App/ProjectImport.swift's bar — whose denominator is an archive's compressed size, hence "of about" — this one is simply the truth. The file line is the frame currently open, truncated from the HEAD so the leaf name stays readable. THE IOS-ONLY LINE is "Keep LetsLapse open": iOS suspends network activity in the background, so that is the platform rule rather than advice, and the sentence after it is what makes the rule survivable — nothing joins the library until every file has landed, so being interrupted costs the transfer and nothing else. macOS says only the second half (macOS/library-import.progress.svg). Flow control is a windowed ack: the client acks cumulative bytes every 8 MB and the server never runs more than 32 MB ahead of what has been written to disk — the send completion is NOT a drain signal, and a semaphore built on it let a whole project buffer into memory. Measured iPad Air M3 ← iPhone over Wi-Fi (2026-08-28): serving footprint flat at 69 MB across a 7.3 GB / 2,869-file project. Cancel sends a cancel frame, the server stops between chunks, and the staged tree is discarded — there is no resume in this phase, so a partial is disk nobody could spend. TERMINAL STATES, desc-only: "Import complete — “name” was added to your library" with Import another / Done (macOS/library-import.done.svg draws it); and "Couldn't import" with the server's sentence verbatim and Try again — including the storage refusal, which is checked BEFORE a byte moves and is also flagged on the project row itself, because on a 128 GB phone that is the common case rather than the edge one.

g.text: Keep LetsLapse open — iOS pauses transfers in the
background. Nothing joins your library until every file has
landed, so stopping leaves no half-project behind.
